# A map of the review and this book {#sec-coverage}

This map is an audit of **topic coverage**, not a claim to reproduce the review's sentences, figures, or every historical citation. All substantive sections of the published review and its publicly accessible author manuscript are represented. The review's contents and section names provide the navigation below [@zaburdaev2015]. The book groups related arguments to support a first reading; detailed derivations, computational checks, exercises, and the mathematical toolbox are added teaching material.

## What has been added

The probability and transform primer, explicit dimensional checks, age-structured construction, distinction between no-renewal and total front masses, fresh-start MSD constants, marginal logarithms, worked exercises, executable Julia experiments, original vector figures, and publication validation make the book independently usable. Chapter 10 is a laboratory guide, not a replacement for the analytical derivations.

Some formulas depend on choices that a broad review may suppress for readability. This book explicitly distinguishes iid direction redraws from mandatory flips, stationary from fresh preparation, the central limit from the ballistic-scale limit, and finite-time measures from limiting densities. Where an application uses a more general model, the changed assumptions are stated before importing a scaling law.

## Scope of completeness

Covering the review means treating its scientific subjects and explaining the main mechanisms and mathematical results, with enough background to follow their use here. It does not mean reproducing its approximately 300-item bibliography or transcribing every reported parameter, historical attribution, and plot. Numerical or experimental claims are attached to primary sources where they are used. A reader seeking the precise original data or apparatus should consult those sources, just as they would for any course textbook.
